name: Glymur waterfall
region: Botnsdalur, at the head of Hvalfjörður, west Iceland
why: Through a cave, over the river on a log, and up the edge of a 198 m gorge to look straight down Iceland's second-highest fall.
book: Free, car park at the end of the Botnsdalur road (off Route 47). The log and its cable over the Botnsá are in place only from about June to September.
water: The Botnsá above the fall is clean; carry water for the climb.
dangers: Steep drops at the gorge edge with no railing; slippery after rain.
Ropes on the steepest rocky steps.
The upper ford above the fall is knee-deep and cold, impossible after heavy rain: if so, go back the way you came.
turnaround: If the Botnsá runs high at the log, do not cross: the view from the cave side ends there.

points.name: Glymur car park, Botnsdalur
points.note: At the end of the valley road; the path follows the Botnsá east through birch scrub.

points.name: Þvottahellir cave
points.note: The path drops through a lava cave down to the river.

points.name: Log crossing on the Botnsá
points.note: A log with a steel cable to hold on to, just above the water; then the climb up the west rim begins.

points.name: Glymur gorge viewpoint
points.note: From the rim the 198 m fall plunges into a narrow mossy gorge; ford the river above it and come down the east side.
